table_name: Table 7A - Requirements for Firefighting Installations - For Residential Buildings
band_matching_convention: Each band's 'structured_criteria.match_any' is a list of clauses; a case matches the band if it satisfies ALL keys within any one clause (AND within a clause, OR across clauses). 'confidence': 'explicit' means the source text gave this range directly; 'interpreted' means the source's compound phrasing (a height threshold OR an area range, presented together under one heading) was resolved by treating a height threshold alone as escalating to the higher-numbered band even below the area threshold - this interpretation has NOT been confirmed against the literal table layout in the source PDF and should be signed off by a fire-safety domain expert before being trusted as ground truth in a production report.

notes: If the building has a kitchen, protection level upgrades to HL-2.
If the building has a basement requiring sprinkler protection, protection level upgrades to CL-3.
If the building has EV parks in podium/basement, must be sprinklered and comply with CL-5.
Rate-of-rise heat detection required in EV parking/charging areas; smoke detectors in all basements except ICE vehicle parks (which get CO sensors to activate ventilation).
If building height exceeds 60 m, hydraulic calculations with multi-level pumping/storage and gravity-redundant down-comer should be considered; pumps should not exceed 12 bar shutoff pressure.
Pump pressure/quantity must be supported by hydraulic calculations.

Cluster of up to 5 buildings (not closer than 9 m, no shared EV basement): 2500 lpm at 10 bar common pumping, 255000 litre water storage. If buildings are closer than 9 m or EV parking/charging is in a shared basement, protection level must comply with CL-5.
Multi-level pumping/storage per SLD may be considered for cluster buildings over 45 m; water storage at every 45 m above should be provided per building.
If cluster exceeds 5 buildings, another set of pumps/storage of similar capacity is required (max 2 such sets recommended, subject to hydraulic requirements at the remotest point).
